open.heading:
Four papers
{{nobody has to sit}}
body: None of the programmes below is compulsory, and none of them counts towards a board result. That is what makes entering them a decision — and the school names which ones it enters rather than describing a culture of enrichment in the abstract.

What each asks for is different in kind, which is the useful part for a family reading this: one is a written talent search, one is a defended project, one is an original idea, and one is a paper set from the primary years.
What has come back from them — the national qualifications and the placings — is recorded on [Olympiad Achievements](/academics/student-success/olympiad-achievements/) rather than repeated here.

list.heading:
A search, a defence,
{{an idea, a paper}}
body: Read side by side, the four programmes ask for four different things — and between them they cover most of what a science education is supposed to produce. A student who can sit a talent search may not be the one who can defend a project in front of a panel.

Where the work is actually done is on [STEM, Robotics & Enrichment](/academics/teaching-learning/stem-robotics/); CUET destinations are on [University Counselling](/academics/student-success/university-counselling/).
From time to time the school enables participation in other nationally notified science and academic programmes. It does not publish them as a standing list, so none is named here.

cells.label: Vidyarthi Vigyan Manthan
cells.value: The national science talent search, for students of **Classes VI to XI**. A written search, sat against a national field.

cells.label: National Children’s Science Congress
cells.value: Project-based science — work **presented and defended**, not answered on a paper.

cells.label: Inspire Award MANAK
cells.value: The Department of Science & Technology’s scheme for **original ideas** from school students, taken to national level.

cells.label: Science Olympiad Foundation
cells.value: The olympiad, entered **from the primary years upward** — the earliest external paper a Sunbeam child sits.

cells.label: CUET (UG)
cells.value: The senior-school entrance examination; the school published 2025 results across PCM, Commerce and Humanities.

cells.label: VVM
cells.value: A written search for scientific temper and reasoning.

cells.label: NCSC
cells.value: Investigate, innovate and present — then defend it.

cells.label: INSPIRE MANAK
cells.value: Original ideas from school students, taken to national level.

cells.label: Olympiads
cells.value: External academic assessments from the primary years upward.

close.heading:
Named,
{{so it can be checked.}}
body: The school names the programmes it enters and the classes eligible for them. It does not publish a coaching timetable, how students are selected for entry, or whether preparation runs inside or outside the school day — and none of that is invented here.
